summary.en: Pakistan has suspended the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provincial government led by Imran Khan's party, labeling the move a coup, while security forces in Kurram repelled a cross-border infiltration, killing one Pakistani soldier and twelve militants, including Afghan Taliban fighters. A Houthi missile strike hit Riyadh airport, killing a Pakistani national and wounding eleven others. The Taliban are exploiting European fears of migrants, and Afghanistan announced a potential China trade route to the Persian Gulf. The conflict remains deadly, with 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Pakistan har suspendert provinsregjeringen i Khyber Pakhtunkhwa ledet av Imran Khans parti, og betegner tiltaket som et kupp, mens sikkerhetsstyrker i Kurram avverget en grensekrypning, drepte en pakistansk soldat og tolv militante, inkludert afghanske Taliban-krigere. Et houthi-missilangrep traff Riyadh-flyplassen, drepte en pakistansk statsborger og såret elleve andre. Taliban utnytter europeisk frykt for migranter, og Afghanistan kunngjorde en potensiell kinesisk handelsrute til Persiabukta. Konflikten forblir dødelig, med 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
